class.name: HDWIUARTResource
class.brief_description: Virtual UART port the FSW talks to as [code]/dev/ttySIM<port_index>[/code] - e.g. the HASP gondola downlink/uplink link.
class.description:
Models one serial port as a byte pipe with two independent directions; this resource is the device on the far end of the wire. The simulation drains the bytes the FSW transmits and produces the bytes the FSW receives. The two actions are deliberately asymmetric, and that asymmetry is what keeps the kernel's stream framed: [constant UART_WRITE] - FSW [i]to[/i] sim. A pure sink: the payload is appended to [member from_fsw] and [signal on_uart_write] is emitted. This resource [b]never[/b] replies to a write - a response here desyncs the kernel's read loop. [constant UART_READ] - sim [i]to[/i] FSW. A request/response polled roughly every 10 ms per port. This resource [b]always[/b] replies, even with zero bytes: it drains up to [constant UART_READ_MAX_CHUNK] bytes off the front of [member to_fsw] and ships them. The response carries no dev_id (the kernel knows which port it polled); anything not drained stays queued for the next poll. Line config (baud, parity, stop bits) is [i]not[/i] on the wire - the kernel applies termios locally and never forwards it. Model timing engine-side if you need it; HASP is a fixed 4800 8N1 link, so a hard-coded model suffices. [b]How to interface[/b] [olist] [*]Set [member port_index] - the kernel assigns indices by position in the sync body, so this must match that position (the registry emits ports in [member port_index] order to keep them in sync) and is also the [code]ttySIM[/code] minor. Set [member device_name]. [*]Call [method HDWIResource.init] to register the port. [*]Connect [signal on_uart_write] to consume bytes the FSW sends; produce bytes for the FSW by appending to [member to_fsw] via [method queue_to_fsw] (the next [constant UART_READ] delivers them). [*]Connect [signal HDWIResource.on_send] to forward [constant UART_READ] responses to the kernel socket. [/olist] [b]Example - an echo port[/b] [codeblock] var uart = HDWIUARTResource.new() uart.device_name = "hasp0" uart.port_index = 0 uart.init()
uart.on_uart_write.connect(_on_write) uart.on_send.connect(_write_to_kernel_socket)
func _on_write(port_index, data): # Echo whatever the FSW transmitted straight back to it. uart.queue_to_fsw(data) [/codeblock]

method.name: queue_to_fsw
method.description: Appends [param bytes] to [member to_fsw] for the FSW to receive on its next read. Convenience wrapper around assigning [member to_fsw].

method.name: handle_uart_write
method.description: Internal. Appends [param payload] to [member from_fsw] and emits [signal on_uart_write]. Sends no response. Invoked by [method HDWIResource.dispatch_action] for [constant UART_WRITE].

method.name: handle_uart_read
method.description: Internal. Emits [signal on_uart_read] (synchronous, so GDScript can top up [member to_fsw]), drains up to [constant UART_READ_MAX_CHUNK] bytes off the front of [member to_fsw], frames them, and emits [signal HDWIResource.on_send] - always, even if zero bytes are available. Invoked by [method HDWIResource.dispatch_action] for [constant UART_READ].

method.name: get_group_type_representation
method.description: Builds the UART section of the [code]CMD_SYNCH[/code] registration body: [code][type][count][/code] followed by each port's 32-byte name, emitted in [member port_index] order so kernel-assigned indices line up. UART carries no extra per-port fields.

method.name: lookup_uart_device_id
method.description: Returns the 0-based registry slot of the port with the given [member port_index], or [code]-1[/code] if none is registered.

members.member: Natural identifier on the wire (inner UART header [code]port_index[/code]) and the [code]/dev/ttySIM<port_index>[/code] minor. Must match the position the kernel assigns during sync; registration is emitted in this order to guarantee that.

Bytes the FSW has written to this port ([constant UART_WRITE]), accumulated in order. The simulation consumes these; clear by assigning an empty array. Each write also arrives live via [signal on_uart_write].
Bytes queued for the FSW to receive ([constant UART_READ]). Fill via [method queue_to_fsw] or by assigning directly; each read drains up to [constant UART_READ_MAX_CHUNK] bytes off the front.

signal.name: on_uart_write
signal.description: Emitted when the FSW writes [param data] to this port. One FSW [code]write()[/code] may arrive as several chunks (the kernel caps each at 256 bytes on a ring-wrap boundary); concatenate in order. No response is sent for a write.

signal.name: on_uart_read
signal.description: Emitted on every [constant UART_READ] poll, before [member to_fsw] is drained, giving GDScript a last chance to top it up synchronously. A reply is always sent afterward, even if no bytes are available.

constants.constant: Largest chunk a single [constant UART_READ] reply will drain off [member to_fsw]. Bounds one poll; the remainder stays queued for the next.
